{{Quote|Premonitions&hellip; Premonitions&hellip; deep questions they are. Sense the future, once all Jedi could; now few alone have the skill. Visions&hellip; gifts from the Force, and curses.|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith novel'']]</ref>}}
'''Force visions''' were rare&mdash;but powerful&mdash;aspects of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], and considered the cornerstone of the [[Unifying Force/Legends|Unifying Force]]. They were among the greatest of [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]].

==Overview==
{{Quote|I have seen the Temple in ruins, the Senate smashed, and Coruscant itself shattered by orbital bombardment from immense ships of impossible design. I have seen Coruscant, the seat of galactic culture, become a jungle far more hostile and alien than any on Haruun Kal. I have seen the end of civilization.|[[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], foreseeing the [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|Battle of Coruscant]]|<ref name="Shatterpoint (novel)">[[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']]</ref>}}
[[File:MuurTalismanVision.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Feln]], [[Q'Anilia]], and [[Xamar]]'s vision about the [[Muur Talisman]].]]
Generally, when peering deep into the Force, a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force user]] had the potential to see events that could happen in the future. Force visions were extremely rare, and uncontrollable. Often, one would meditate to gain a vision, but only a few would succeed. [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and his descendants, particularly his son, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]], and his grandsons, [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] and [[Ben Skywalker]], were often prone to Force Visions. They were known to occur sometimes in a Jedi padawan's [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Trial of the Spirit]], preparatory to [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Knighthood]].

[[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] felt that visions were of great importance to the Force, and often acted on them as best he could. However, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] warned that the future was always in motion and that its events were only ''possible''. As such, interpreting a vision by oneself was generally considered dangerous.

Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], for example, beheld in vision his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], but as "an elder man, alone, living on a [[Tatooine/Legends|desolate planet]], his only companions his dark memories." Even so, Qui-Gon had to remind himself, as Yoda taught, that "''the future is not fixed, but fluid'' ...'' ''Visions did not have to come true."<ref name=":0">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Fight for Truth]]''</ref>

Amongst Jedi, the [[Jedi Seer]]s of the Order were responsible for the majority of visions, and interpreted them for [[Jedi Consular]]s. Following the destruction and subsequent [[New Jedi Order|reconstruction]] of the Order, the [[Jedi Council of Seers]] took up this role.

Some Jedi and [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] endowed with this Force power were capable of detecting when friends and apprentices were in danger, examining details of past events, and predicting the probable outcome of future actions or events.

Vision-prone Sith, such as [[Kreia|Darth Traya]], could peer into the future many thousands of years and predict events with great accuracy. In this way, Traya was able to foretell the death of the [[Jango Fett/Legends|last]] of the Mandalorians at the hands of a [[Mace Windu/Legends|Jedi]].

But unlike the Jedi, the Sith believed&mdash;based on experience, or perhaps more often, on their own arrogant self-conception&mdash;that visions would always come to pass, that they must unfailingly endeavor to make them realities. Some Sith would even combine their own ideas of what might come to be into their visions.

[[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] was perhaps the most vision-prone [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] in [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|history]] and used his visionary gifts to ensure his own [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY/Legends|election]] as [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]], and his ascension as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]]. Regarding his visions, Emperor Palpatine consulted with the [[Prophets of the Dark Side]], a Sith splinter group that was dedicated to studying the future through the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].

Force visions were not necessarily limited to the Jedi and Sith, however. Others in the galaxy also experienced visions that might be attributed, it could be argued, to the Force, or "[[Ashla]]," or whatever a given culture might call ''the essential force behind all life in the universe''. [[O-Vieve]], the [[Benevolent Guide]] of [[Kegan/Legends|Kegan]], for example, saw visions (which Qui-Gon Jinn could not discount) that foretold the coming of a great darkness that surrounded and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|emanated from]] the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]]&mdash;an evil that would spread to "[[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|engulf]]" the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]&mdash;but also glimpses or "flashes" of an ominous, destructive future event: "an [[Death Star/Legends|explosive device]] sent to destroy an [[Alderaan/Legends|entire planet]] without a shiver" and "[[Stormtrooper/Legends|masked soldiers]]" who would bring "fear and suffering." O-Vieve foresaw an [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|invasion]] of [[Palpatine/Legends|evil]] that would "[[Galactic Empire/Legends|cloak]] [entire planets] like a black cloud."<ref name=":0" />

But as Yoda taught, ever reminding those in his stewardship of this one constant in what was both a phenomenon and gift, Force vision would continue to have its limitations due to the factors of ''multiple possibilities'' or ''outcomes'' in any forecast of the future.

For example, in [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]], sixteen-year-old Anakin Skywalker experienced three different incarnations of the same Force vision, the general interpretation of which the Jedi Padawan thought he understood, though not its specifics; but as his Master Obi-Wan Kenobi and Yoda ''both'' warned, there were elements in the dream that came to mean something entirely different from what Skywalker initially interpreted them as meaning. The vision's last manifestation had come to him just after having surfaced from an afternoon swim in the indoor lake at the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], near the [[Room of a Thousand Fountains/Legends|Room of a Thousand Fountains]].

In the vision, he saw himself commanding a massive fleet; he witnessed a [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] revolt of hundreds shouting his name; he beheld his mother, [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi]], in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] embracing him and heard the sound of her binding cuffs drop to the ground at the touch of his hand upon them. As the vision ended, Anakin knew he'd somehow lost his mother forever, and everyone he'd ever loved. Finally, he heard the echo of strange words: ''The One Below remains below''. While Skywalker immediately confided the dream to his Master, neither Jedi was clear about its meaning. But when they consulted [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] Yoda, the ancient Jedi sage gave the meaning of ''the One Below ''as being a [[Koban]] title, referring to the centuries-long imprisonment by [[Advozse/Legends|Advozsec]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] of [[Yaddle/Legends|Yaddle]], the revered Jedi Master who was of the same species as Yoda. That she was about to leave on a very troubling [[Mission to Mawan|mission to the planet Mawan]] was no coincidence: Yoda felt that Anakin's dream was a ''warning'' and the answer to the Council's debate about which Jedi team to send with her to address the grave situation that existed there. The visionary Padawan was disappointed at his dream's interpretation, for he had hoped that the time had come at last when he might "step out of [[Dream/Legends|his dreams]]" and return to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] to free the slaves, but most importantly, his own mother.<ref name="Jedi Quest: The Shadow Trap">''[[Jedi Quest: The Shadow Trap]]''</ref>

As it turned out, however, by mission's end, Anakin understood that his original interpretation of the vision emanated from what he ''wanted'' the vision to signify, based on his own wishes, hopes, desires. The binding cuffs that clamored to the floor, in fact, turned out to be ''his own ''cuffs, falling to the ground at his liberation by Master Yaddle from the captivity of [[Force void/Legends|Void in the Force]] [[Granta Omega]]. Skywalker's conviction that his vision revealed that he stood to lose everyone he'd ever loved also took on a new meaning: for he'd come to deeply admire and value Master Yaddle, who ultimately chose to [[Death/Legends|perish]] for all the inhabitants of the planet's capital city of [[Naatan]], including her fellow Jedi, when she sacrificed herself by creating a Force implosion to absorb into her own being the deadly [[Poison/Legends|toxins]] of an Omega-created [[Dihexalon gas|dihexalon]] [[Bomb/Legends|bomb]]. Personal desire, as Anakin discovered, could cloud, then, a Force vision's true meaning, just as Yoda had forewarned.

Ego, when combined with power, was also, it seems, a factor that "clouded" visions: Palpatine, in his visions, never saw himself die. [[Darth Caedus]] also saw many possible outcomes in his future, yet none of them involved his death. Notwithstanding, [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]] was able to ''calculate'' the future and foresee his own death, professing that this limitation could be ''overcome'' if one's skill in it was prodigious enough.<ref name="The Tenebrous Way">{{InsiderCite|130|The Tenebrous Way}}</ref>

[[Precognition/Legends|''Precognition'']], ''[[Force sight]]'', and ''[[Farsight/Legends|farsight]]'' were forms of Force vision.
